#   remote_noop / remote_incr        noop / incr with -O localhost -T

# RATCHET-DOWN-ONLY RULE: these budgets may only ever DECREASE. When an
# optimization lands and the observed counts drop, lower max to
# ceil(new-observed * 1.15) in the same change. Never raise a budget to make
# a regression pass; a budget failure means the change reintroduced
# per-run process spawns or structural work that was pinned away.
# EXACT ROWS: ssh_connections and ssh_master_opens are pinned at exactly
# the observed count, with no headroom, and checked in both directions:
# every new ssh connection costs a full handshake, so one extra connection
# is a regression, and a lower count means a scenario stopped reaching ssh
# the way it should. Lower them only when a change really opens fewer
# Never budget advisory:* rows (wall time is timing noise, not a contract).
# History: seeded 2026-06-10 (noop TOTAL=176, dryrun_incr TOTAL=38 with the
# original 12-tool list), re-ratcheted 2026-06-11 after the per-run temp root
# (noop 43 / dryrun 9), 2026-06-12 after the fast no-op proof (noop 30), and
# 2026-06-13 after the proof moved to regular files (dirs_created 0).
# Re-seeded 2026-09-01 with two deliberate metric changes, both justified by
#   1. The counted tool list widened from 12 to 22 helpers (adds cat rm mv ls
#      mkdir cmp wc id stat uname). The old list never saw the hot path: a
#      26-dataset live incremental run spawned 860 stat + 430 id (run-root
#      revalidation on every temp file) and 300 cat + 214 rm (stage-file
#      readback/cleanup) while every budgeted tool stayed flat. TOTAL rows
#      therefore rise (noop 30->51 observed, dryrun_incr 8->15) purely from
#      the newly counted tools; every pre-existing per-tool row kept its old
#      ceiling or ratcheted down (mktemp 2->0, tr stays 0).
#   2. A third scenario, incr (live incremental, one receive per dataset),
#      pins the per-dataset hot path that noop/dryrun never exercised. Seeded
#      after the run-root revalidation fix and the once-per-pass destination
#      view (recursive destination listings 28->3): observed incr TOTAL=1129
#      full / 483 small, dominated by tr 338 cat 277 rm 214 awk 209 per-dataset
#      spawns that the discovery/reconcile collapse is expected to remove.
#      incr profile rows scale with dataset count, so full and small differ.

# Re-ratcheted 2026-09-26 (next phase W6). The path-security metadata read
# moved from the GNU/BSD stat fallbacks to one portable `ls -ldin`: whole-root
# removal reads the run root's inode, owner and mode with one ls instead of
# two stat calls on BSD (the failing `stat -c`, then `stat -f`), so every
# scenario swaps stat 2 for ls 1. The ls ceilings rise from 0 to 1 and the
# stat ceilings fall from 3 to 0: a tool swap, not added work (GNU stat
# needed one spawn, so Linux trades stat 1 for ls 1). Equal -O and -T specs
# now share one capability probe, so the remote scenarios make one ssh call,
# one uname and one probe temp file fewer. -V measurements on macOS: noop
# ceil(observed * 1.15); ssh_connections and ssh_master_opens are unchanged.
